steps.title: Tinta Negra
steps.body: Tinta Negra is a black grape making about 80% of Madeira. It's versatile, used for every sweetness level. Until 2015, it couldn't be named on labels; now it can. Most Madeira labelled by age, like 5 Years Old, is Tinta Negra, unless a noble grape is named.

steps.title: The noble grapes
steps.body: Four white grapes are called noble, and each traditionally gives a level of sweetness: Sercial, driest; Verdelho, medium dry; Boal, or Bual, medium sweet; Malvasia, or Malmsey, sweetest. A wine named after a noble grape must contain at least 85% of it. Terrantez, rare, is a fifth noble grape, medium dry to medium sweet.

steps.prompt: Order the noble grapes from driest to sweetest.

steps.body: All Madeira keeps striking acidity, even the sweetest Malmsey. That's what makes it so fresh and long-lived.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Tinta Negra makes about 80% of Madeira
Sercial, Verdelho, Boal and Malvasia run from dry to sweet
Named noble grape wines need at least 85% of that grape
